candidate: uniform-reference full relative entropy on the antipodal W5 record at fixed norm
purpose: Test an explicit P-and-icosahedron selector mechanism without fitting a quark mass, introducing a free coefficient, or promoting a conjectured source law to an axiom.

source_structure.carrier: twelve icosahedral ports in six antipodal pairs
source_structure.record: a bounded observer-like self-reading patch has local port records, readback and a public probability record; only its declared classical antipodal scalar record is modeled here, not a general quantum state
source_structure.P_role: No numerical P is consumed. The result holds for every admissible amplitude, hence for any scalar amplitude map r(P). Such a map is not derived here.

fixed_assumptions_not_derived_from_core: antipodal scalar records on the twelve-port carrier
selection by full relative entropy at a fixed quadratic norm
the quadrupole spectral attachment to a three-family mass operator

global_argument: At each fixed purity the feasible closed simplex is compact and the objective extends continuously to zero, so a minimum exists.

For 0<r<sqrt(60), a boundary point cannot minimize the objective. If two positive coordinates differ, adding epsilon at a zero and changing those coordinates by O(epsilon) preserves sum and purity by the implicit function theorem. The new coordinate contributes epsilon*log(epsilon), while existing positive coordinates change by O(epsilon).

If all k positive boundary coordinates equal 1/k with 2<=k<=5, give each the base (1-epsilon)/k and displace two by plus/minus delta, with delta^2=epsilon/k-(k+1)*epsilon^2/(2*k); put epsilon at a previously zero coordinate. Sum and purity remain exact. The opposite displacements cancel their O(sqrt(epsilon)) first-order entropy terms, so the old-coordinate entropy change is O(epsilon), whereas epsilon*log(epsilon) is negative and dominant. The k=1 case occurs only at r=sqrt(60).

At an interior stationary point the two constraint gradients are independent unless r=0. Lagrange stationarity reads log(p_i)+1=lambda+2*mu*p_i. Strict concavity of log(x) implies at most two positive roots a<b.

If b occurs at least twice, the direction (1,-1) on two b coordinates is tangent to both constraints. Its constrained second variation is 2*(1/b-log(b/a)/(b-a)). This is strictly negative because, for t=b/a>1, log(t)-1+1/t has value zero at one and derivative (t-1)/t^2>0.

Thus an interior minimum has one high and five equal low coordinates. Solving its two constraints gives p_H=(1+5*r/sqrt(60))/6 and p_L=(1-r/sqrt(60))/6. Compactness, boundary exclusion and stationarity prove this is the only minimum up to permutation.

The endpoints are the uniform distribution at r=0 and a one-point distribution at r=sqrt(60). At zero every normalized direction a is equivalent as a probability record, no direction is selected, and the actual quadrupole r*Q is zero. Every winner at nonzero r selects one of the six antipodal axes and has a quadrupole with one double eigenvalue. An unoriented fivefold axis has a D5 stabilizer of order ten.

physical_boundary.quadrupole: Q = 2*sum_i a_i*(n_i*n_i^T-I/3), with six unit icosahedral axis representatives; this forward map obeys n_i^T Q n_i = (8/5)*a_i, not a_i
physical_boundary.conditional_mass_consequence: A single quadrupole spectral readout retains the double eigenvalue, so this mechanism cannot supply three unequal masses in either sector for any scalar r(P).
physical_boundary.scope_exclusion: Only this full-entropy fixed-norm antipodal-record mechanism and its single-quadrupole spectral readout are excluded. General OPH completions, different source constraints, multiple coupled records and independently derived physical readouts are not excluded.

input_policy.discovery_status: exploratory mechanism-level theorem; existing mass hierarchy knowledge motivates the question, so this is not a blind discovery
